item.title: Press Coverage: Ohio State Still Favored to Win National Championship Despite Challenging College Football Playoff Path As No. 2 Seed
item.description: Ohio State digested its Indiana loss in a span of 16 hours. The Buckeyes will dive into the film, review their flaws and work to address them. Otherwise, it's College Football Playoff time. Ryan Day's squad learned its seeding and quarterfinal location on Sunday, as the Buckeyes earned the No. 2 spot in the CFP and will play in the Cotton Bowl against either No. 7 Texas A&M or No. 10 Miami. item.title: Ohio State Placed in Cotton Bowl Over Orange Bowl to Avoid Possible Home Game for Miami
item.description: Ohio State will play in the Cotton Bowl rather than the Orange Bowl to avoid the possibility of the Buckeyes having to play Miami in the Hurricanes’ home stadium. With No. 1 seed Indiana contracted to the Rose Bowl as the Big Ten champion and No. 3 seed Georgia contracted to the Sugar Bowl as the SEC champion, the College Football Playoff selection committee’s decision on where to send No. 2 seed Ohio State for its quarterfinal came down to Dallas and Miami. item.title: Where, When and How to Get Tickets to Ohio State’s College Football Playoff Quarterfinal Game at the Cotton Bowl
item.description: Ohio State is back on its quest to repeat as national champions. The Buckeyes hit a bump in the road, suffering their first loss of the season to No. 1 Indiana, but still grabbed the No. 2 seed in the College Football Playoff and will face the winner of No. 7 Texas A&M and No. 10 Miami in the Cotton Bowl. item.title: Ohio State Safety Caleb Downs Wins 2025 Lott IMPACT Trophy
item.description: Caleb Downs is a great player, on and off the field. Widely regarded as one of the best defensive players in college football and a captain for the Buckeyes this season, Downs is a leader for Ohio State, on and off the field. Sunday night was yet another example of that, as Downs was awarded the Lott IMPACT Trophy. item.title: Snap Counts: Ohio State Leans on Starters in Big Ten Championship Game As Only Four Backups Play More Than 12 Snaps
item.description: A close game in which Ohio State trailed in the second half for the first time all season before ultimately losing meant minimal playing time for most of the Buckeyes’ backups. Ohio State leaned heavily on its starters in the Big Ten Championship Game. Only four players who didn’t start the game played more than 12 snaps against Indiana: defensive tackle Eddrick Houston (31), right guard Gabe VanSickle (29), tight end Bennett Christian (23) and wide receiver Brandon Inniss (21). item.description: Although he’ll remain with Ohio State for the duration of its College Football Playoff run, Brian Hartline was officially introduced as South Florida’s new head coach on Monday. Following the Buckeyes’ Big Ten Championship Game loss on Saturday, the Ohio State offensive coordinator and wide receivers coach flew to Tampa on Sunday to get started at USF. item.title: Ohio State Quarterback Julian Sayin Named Finalist for 2025 Heisman Trophy
item.description: For the fifth time in eight years, Ohio State’s starting quarterback is a Heisman Trophy finalist. Julian Sayin is one of four finalists for the 2025 Heisman Trophy along with Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza, Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love and Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia.
